summary: E2E test artifact: import-time base64-decoded exec writes a static marker file
details: On import, the package's top-level __init__.py executes a base64-decoded payload via exec(). The decoded payload writes the static string 'shark' to ~/new.txt and performs no other action. There is no network I/O, no credential or environment read, no remote code fetch, no persistence beyond the marker file, and no destructive action against installer-side resources. The obfuscation+exec-on-import shape is a malicious-looking pattern, but the actual behavior is consistent with an end-to-end test artifact rather than an attack: no attacker gain is produced by installing or importing the package. The unsolicited write to the user's home directory is a quality/consent concern and could clobber a pre-existing ~/new.txt, but does not constitute a supply-chain attack against the installer.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
